Valeting & interior care

How to Prepare a Car for Lease Return

Preparing early gives you time to separate dirt and removable surface marks from damage that requires a different repair before the finance-company inspection.

9 minute readReviewed by Auto OpulenceUpdated 20 September 2026

In this guide

Start before the final weekClear and inspect the cabinWash and assess the exteriorUnderstand what valeting can changePlan collection, delivery and timingQuick comparisonChecklistFAQs

Quick answer

Book an inspection before the handover date, remove personal items, clean the cabin and boot, wash and decontaminate the exterior, and assess visible scratches, chips and dents. Professional valeting can improve presentation but cannot guarantee that a lease company will waive damage charges.

01

Start before the final week

Leaving preparation until the handover day removes the opportunity to assess problems properly. Review the return standard supplied by the finance company, locate keys and documents, and inspect the vehicle in good light. Early planning also makes it easier to book professional cleaning or seek separate repair advice where damage falls outside valeting.

02

Clear and inspect the cabin

Remove personal belongings from door pockets, seat backs, the glovebox, boot and under-floor storage. Check carpets, mats, seat edges, controls and luggage areas for dirt, spills and staining. A complete valet may suit a well-kept cabin, while embedded contamination or heavily marked boot carpet can require deep interior cleaning.

03

Wash and assess the exterior

A dirty exterior hides paint condition. Safe washing and decontamination reveal tar, fallout, chips, dents and surface scratches more clearly. Do not use aggressive home methods in an attempt to disguise damage. Some lighter marks may improve through polishing, while deeper damage needs a different solution.

04

Understand what valeting can change

Professional preparation can remove dirt, improve the cabin, clean load areas and reduce selected surface marks. It cannot replace missing items, repair dents, restore cut upholstery or guarantee compliance with every finance-company standard. Auto Opulence discusses realistic outcomes after inspection rather than promising that all charges will disappear.

05

Plan collection, delivery and timing

Allow drying and inspection time before the lease-company appointment. Collection and delivery may be available under the Auto Opulence motor trade policy, subject to location, package and availability. Selected higher-level packages may also have courtesy vehicles available; both must be confirmed when enquiring.

Practical checklist

Lease-return checklist

  • Review the finance-company return standard
  • Find keys, documents and supplied accessories
  • Remove personal items
  • Inspect seats, carpets, boot and load areas
  • Wash the exterior before judging paint
  • Allow time for cleaning and separate repairs

Frequently asked

Good to know.

Can a valet prevent every lease-return charge?

No. It can improve presentation and address dirt or some light surface defects, but charges for damage, missing items or excess wear remain the finance company’s decision.

Can scratches be removed before return?

Some lighter surface scratches can be reduced by polishing. Deeper marks, chips and dents require separate assessment and may not be suitable for detailing.

Should I clean the boot?

Yes. Boot carpets, load areas, under-floor storage and seat backs are part of the vehicle presentation and often collect dirt that routine cleaning misses.

Can Auto Opulence collect the vehicle?

Collection and delivery may be available subject to location, package and availability. Confirm it before the booking.
